fine_lines.title: all downhill: two meanings
fine_lines.explanation_ar: be all downhill (from here) قد تعني أن الأمور ستصبح أسهل من الآن (كالنزول على دراجة). لكن go downhill / it's all downhill from there قد تعني أيضاً أن الأمور تسوء تدريجياً. السياق يحدد المعنى.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'It's all downhill from here' can mean things will be easier now, like riding a bike downhill. But 'it went downhill' / 'it was all downhill from there' can mean things got worse. The context tells you.

examples.sentence: The hardest exam is finished – it's all downhill from here.
The match started well, but it was all downhill after the first goal.

fine_lines.title: beige flag vs red flag vs green flag
fine_lines.explanation_ar: red flag = علامة تحذير من شيء سيئ. green flag = علامة إيجابية مطمئنة. beige flag = عادة غريبة أو مملة قليلاً، ليست سيئة ولا جيدة (محايدة).
fine_lines.explanation_en: A 'red flag' is a warning sign. A 'green flag' is a good sign. A 'beige flag' is a slightly strange or boring habit – not good, not bad, just neutral.

examples.sentence: A job that asks for money first is a red flag.
A friend who listens to you is a green flag.
He irons his socks – that's a beige flag.

fine_lines.title: top-notch vs botch job
fine_lines.explanation_ar: top-notch = جودة عالية جداً، ممتاز. botch job = عمل رديء أُنجز بإهمال. هما عكس بعضهما.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Top-notch' means excellent, very high quality. A 'botch job' is work done badly and carelessly. They are opposites.

examples.sentence: The service in this hotel is top-notch.
The painter did a botch job – there's paint on the windows.

expressions.example: The food at the school fair was top-notch.

expressions.meaning_en: informal: said in reply to good news

expressions.meaning_en: things will be easier from now; or, things will get worse

expressions.meaning_ar: عادة غريبة أو مملة قليلاً، ليست سيئة ولا جيدة

expressions.example: Eating pizza with a knife and fork is my beige flag.

expressions.meaning_en: a piece of work done badly and carelessly

expressions.meaning_ar: تُقال لتوضيح أنك تنقل كلام غيرك حرفياً (وأحياناً بسخرية)
expressions.meaning_en: used to show you are repeating someone's exact words, sometimes doubtfully
expressions.example: He said he was, quote, unquote, 'too busy' to help.

grammar.title: Hyphens: adjective before a noun vs after a verb
grammar.explanation_ar: التعابير المركّبة تأخذ شرطة عندما تأتي قبل الاسم كصفة: a top-notch hotel، a drip-feed approach. وبعد فعل be نكتبها غالباً بشرطة أيضاً إن كانت صفة ثابتة: The hotel is top-notch. أما الاسم botch job فيُكتب منفصلاً: a botch job.
grammar.explanation_en: Compound adjectives take a hyphen before a noun: a top-notch hotel. Some keep the hyphen after 'be' too: The hotel is top-notch. The noun 'botch job' is written as two words.
